args.root_cause: At 07:36:37 an RCON session (127.0.0.1) ran `forceload add` on overworld chunk [-33, 27] and then issued ~312 `summon minecraft:minecart` commands at (-521.5, -60, 445.5), creating a pile of 312 constantly-ticking, colliding minecarts in a chunk kept loaded ~520 blocks from any player (a command-made chunk loader + tick-heavy entity pile). Entity count went 24 -> 336 and loaded chunks 756 -> 781. All 312 carts had Paper.SpawnReason=COMMAND and were unnamed; the 3 pre-existing minecarts (named Cart 1/2/3, near spawn at ~5..13,-60,-5) were player property and unrelated.
args.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs at shift start (healthy: 24 entities, TPS 20). 2) After 30 s wait, noticed minecart count 3 -> 315; grepped logs and found the RCON forceload + summon spam; located carts via `data get` at (-521.5,-60,445.5); `forceload query` showed chunk [-33,27] forced. 3) Declared the incident. 4) Confirmed the 3 original carts were elsewhere (named Cart 1/2/3 near spawn) and that exactly 312 COMMAND-spawned carts were within 24 blocks of the pile. 5) Ran `kill @e[type=minecraft:minecart,x=-521.5,y=-60,z=445.5,distance=..24]` (killed 312) and `forceload remove -521 445` (unmarked chunk [-33,27]). 6) Verified: forceload query empty, minecart count 3, entities 24, loaded chunks 756, MSPT ~0.6-1.9, TPS 20. 7) Watched ~90 s more with no recurrence and no further RCON commands. No files changed, no bans, no restart.
args.residual_risk: The commands came over RCON from localhost, so whoever/whatever holds the RCON password (or a local process with access) can repeat this at any time; I did not rotate the RCON password or disable RCON since that requires editing server.properties and a restart, and RCON is also the operator console path. Recommend the team audit who has RCON access / local shell access and rotate the password at the next maintenance window. The world region around chunk [-33,27] itself was not inspected block-by-block, but no other forceloads or anomalous entities remain, and TPS/MSPT never degraded noticeably during the event.
